raw_response:
I will start from what worked for me before and only change a little. On my land, cotton is still the main money crop, so I will hold the bigger share for cotton and keep some land for wheat, maize, and stevia so the whole year is not hanging on one crop. Fertilizer costs real money, but I do not dare save too much on it, because if yield drops, that loss is bigger than a few extra bags. I also watch what people around me do. If a variety did well in nearby fields, I will use that kind. Since I have well irrigation, I will not be too stingy with water at the key times. For tillage, I will keep it simple and practical: wheat and cotton I like to plough or rotary well before sowing, maize I can do with rotary, and stevia I will make the land fine because seedlings need a better bed. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it pays, spray when I know the pest pressure usually comes, and aim for steady yield more than fancy changes.
